title: Chapter 53: The Chair Is Moving
html:
The driver’s face had gone pale. He forced an awkward laugh. “Well, good luck to you.”

“Thank you. Would you mind stopping the recording now?” Chen Ge gave him what he hoped was a friendly smile. “This is all a misunderstanding.”

“Of course.” The driver readily pressed a button on the console. A few meters later, the red light on his radio came on. He tapped it, and before he could speak, a rough voice crackled through.

“Lao Liu, you’re also near Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy? What is wrong with people tonight? I also have a passenger with me who wants to go there. Actually, we’re quite close. By the way, what is this message that you sent to the group? ‘I am meld postage’?”

“It’s nothing. Pay attention to your passenger.” The driver wiped the sweat from his forehead and hurriedly switched off the radio.

“You meant I am held hostage, didn’t you? Uncle, I thought you trusted me.” Chen Ge raised an eyebrow. Before the man could call the police outright, he added, “You can let me out here.”

“Certainly!” The driver obeyed at once. Even his legs were trembling.

Chen Ge checked that he had everything, climbed out, and closed the door. Only then did he notice the illuminated sign on the taxi’s roof: I AM BEING HELD HOSTAGE. PLEASE CALL THE POLICE!

“Uncle, you sure are creative.”

The taxi sped away as if it had grown wings. Within seconds, silence reclaimed the road for hundreds of meters in every direction. No stars pierced the low rain clouds, and the night threatened a storm. Chen Ge checked his phone. Eight minutes remained.

The man on the radio said he was bringing another passenger to the academy. Who comes here at one in the morning? Could they be connected to my mission?

He reminded himself to stay alert. Without the deadline, he would have hidden in the roadside brush and waited to see who was coming.

Only eight minutes left. I’d better learn the school’s layout. I’ll need every advantage I can get.

Deserted land surrounded Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy. There were no streetlights, only a narrow road cutting through dense forest and undergrowth.

Using his phone as a flashlight, Chen Ge followed the road another hundred meters to the school’s front gate. The chain had rusted to the iron bars, and the gate itself refused to budge. Beyond it lay nothing but darkness.

How do I get in?

He paced before the gate, tossed his backpack over, then retreated several steps. With a running start, he caught the top of the wall and hauled himself across.

The campus was small enough to take in at a glance. Several tall buildings loomed in the darkness like solitary watchmen. Its sign had been removed long ago, and even Chen Ge did not know the school’s true name. Like everyone else in the city, he knew it only as Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy.

Overgrown shrubs had swallowed most of the path. Their branches raked his legs with every step, leaving an irritating mixture of pain and itching.

I’ve managed to arrive within the designated time limit; now my mission is to find Zhang Ya’s red dancing shoes.

Chen Ge pulled the mallet from his backpack. The cold weight of the metal in his hand made him feel safer.

Guided by his phone, he ventured deeper into the school. After only a few steps, something felt wrong. He stopped and tried to backtrack.

Am I imagining this? It feels as if something is pushing me farther inside—and when I step backward, something resists me.

He looked over his shoulder and swept the phone’s light behind him. Nothing was there, neither ghost nor spirit.

Could she already be here? Standing behind me where I can’t see her?Chen Ge shivered. He considered swinging the mallet through the space behind him, then stopped. What if Zhang Ya really is there and I make her angry?

He was only a Haunted House owner, almost defenseless in an abandoned school. The thought of provoking a baleful specter made him shudder.

In any case, I should go in first.

He hitched up his backpack and continued with his phone raised in one hand and the mallet in the other. The darkness deepened. A rising wind carried the first fine drops of rain.

The red dancing shoes are most likely in the dance studio’s girls’ dressing room or Zhang Ya’s old dorm room. I should focus on those two places.

He headed for the nearest building. Neglected trees had twisted into strange shapes, and wild grass reached his waist. Human statues stood scattered across the grounds, lending the darkened campus the atmosphere of a graveyard.

The girls’ dormitory?

The dormitory stood only four stories high, but years of abandonment had made it unsettling. A metal chain secured the glass entrance. Chen Ge leaned close to peer inside.

Every door along the dark corridor was shut. Oddly, a single chair sat in the middle of the hall, facing away from the dorm rooms.

Why leave a single chair in the middle of the corridor? Does it mean something?

Chen Ge drew back from the glass. The front gate and the dormitory are both locked, and there’s no rubbish in the corridor. They must have cleaned the school before closing it. So why leave a chair in the middle of the hall? Was it an accident?

If the school deliberately left it there, what was it meant for? And if the school didn’t, who moved it into the corridor after the building was locked?

He aimed his phone through the glass. The chair stood about five meters inside, directly beneath a broken ceiling light.

The fixture is broken, and the wiring is exposed. A chair beneath a dangling wire… Why does that look like the scene of a hanging?

The longer he studied it, the harder his heart beat.

I’m probably just overthinking.

He glanced around. Wind whispered through the leaves, and the abandoned school seemed to breathe with it.

I can’t scare myself for no reason. Zhang Ya, the Red Specter, is the most terrifying presence in this school. I have her love letter, so who would dare challenge me? It was the only reassurance Chen Ge could find. Besides, this is only an affection mission—a special kind of date. There’s nothing to worry about.

Once the pep talk was over, he approached the glass door with his mallet. He raised it to strike—then noticed something that froze him in place.

The chair was no longer beneath the broken light. It had moved a full meter closer to the entrance.

F*ck!Even Chen Ge had never encountered anything like this. What just happened?
